nodes.question: What are the three approaches used to estimate agriculture's impact on biodiversity in the Brazilian Cerrado?
nodes.answer: The three approaches are the Countryside Species-Area Relationship, Species Threat Abatement and Restoration, and Species Habitat Index.
nodes.paragraph: Article https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-25-57037-9 Choosing t-for-purpose biodiversity impact indicators for agriculture in the BrazilianCerrado ecoregion Gabriela Rabeschini1 ,2,U MartinP e r n3,0 r i sW e S t4& Thomas Kastner1 Understanding and acting on biodiversi ty loss requires robust tools linking biodiversity impacts to land use change , the biggest threat to terrestrial bio- diversity. Here we estimate agriculture S impact on the Brazilian Cerrado S biodiversity using three approaches countryside Species- Area Relationship, Species Threat Abatement and Restorati on and Species Habitat Index. By using same input data, we show how indicator scope and design affects impactassessments and resulting decision-su pport. All indicators show agriculture expansion S increasing pressure on biodiversity. Results suggest that metrics are complementary, providing distinct ly different insight into biodiversity change drivers and impacts. Meaningful ap plications of biodiv ersity indicators therefore require compatibility betwee n focal questions and indicator choice regarding temporal, spatial, and eco logical perspectives on impact and dri- vers. Backward-looking analyses focused on historical land use change landaccountability are best serv ed by the countryside-Spe cies Area Relationship and the Species Habitat Index. Forwar d-looking analyses of impact risk hot- spots and global extinctions mitigatio n are best served by the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration.

nodes.question: Which small mammal species mentioned can be considered a pest in agriculture?
nodes.answer: The common vole (Microtus arvalis) can be considered a pest in agriculture.
nodes.paragraph: Future tests with tube diameters, bait, timing of placement etc. could increase the capture success and demonstrate the applicability of the method to rare species. Also, some training for the involved field workers could be advantageous. Keywords Baited tubes Biodiversity Biomonitoring COI barcoding Wetlands and riparian woodlands Introduction Small mammals status Small mammals are here defined by having a body weight of up to 5 kg following Merritt ( 2010 ) and comprise mainly members of Eulipotyphla, Rodentia and Chiroptera. Some European small mammal species are elusive (e.g., Sicista), some mainly nocturnal (e.g., bats), some rare and of con- servation concern like the European hamster (e.g., Cricetus cricetus), some can be pests in agriculture (e.g., Microtus arvalis; Jacob et al. 2014; Hansson 1992) and some are known to host human pathogenic viruses (e.g., the rodents Clethrionomys glareolus and Apodemus agrarius but also shrews; Bown et al. 2011; Olsson et al. 2002; Ulrich et al. 2009; Vaheri et al. 2013; Weber de Melo et al.

nodes.question: What are some socioeconomic and environmental aspects of silk cocoon production in Brazilian agriculture?
nodes.answer: The socioeconomic and environmental aspects of silk cocoon production in Brazilian agriculture include factors such as labour conditions, natural resource usage, and economic impact on local communities.
